'''''Lemna minuta''''' is a species of [[Lemnoideae|duckweed]] known by the common name '''least duckweed'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=LEMI6|taxon=Lemna minuta|accessdate=24 January 2016}}</ref> It is the smallest ''Lemna'' species.<ref>[http://www.habitas.org.uk/flora/species.asp?item=4649 Flora of Northern Ireland]</ref> It is native to parts of the Americas, and [[introduced species|naturalized]] in others; the exact native range is not known. It is found on other continents as a non-native introduction as well. The plant's distribution is ever-expanding; it has been spreading in Europe and it was described from [[Poland]] for the first time in 2007.<ref>Banaszek, A. and K. Musiał. (2009). [http://www.ib-pan.krakow.pl/pubs-pdf/Acta%20Societatis%20Botanicorum/2009/W69_72.pdf The new kenophyte in Poland - ''Lemna minuta'' Humb., Bonpl., & Kunth] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111004100123/http://www.ib-pan.krakow.pl/pubs-pdf/Acta%20Societatis%20Botanicorum/2009/W69_72.pdf |date=2011-10-04 }}. ''Acta Societatis Botanicorum Poloniae'' 78:1 69-72</ref> In many areas it is a [[noxious weed]], such as in [[Belgium]].<ref name=belg>[http://ias.biodiversity.be/ias/species/show/69 Invasive Alien Species in Belgium: ''Lemna minuta'']</ref>

This tiny plant varies in shape depending on growth conditions. In the shade it is a single green translucent oval body no more than 2.5 millimeters long, and in full sunlight it generally grows in pairs. There is a central vein usually visible under [[magnification]] and [[microscopy]]. The plant produces an ephemeral membrane-bound flower.

This duckweed grows in slow-moving, calm, and stagnant [[freshwater]] habitats. It affects the ecology of its habitat by forming mats on the water surface, reducing sunlight penetration and oxygen exchange.<ref name=belg/>
